children: Uganda's central bank has raised the cash reserve requirement for commercial banks, a move that follows a sharp weakening of the local currency, recently trading near its lowest level in more than two years.
has come under pressure in recent weeks as manufacturers and energy-sector firms boosted demand for dollars to manage higher fuel costs linked to the Middle East conflict.
At 1328 GMT, it traded around 3,925 per dollar, around its weakest level since February 2024, LSEG data showed.
In a circular seen by Reuters on Thursday, the central bank said it had raised the cash reserve requirement for commercial banks to 13.5% from 11.0%.
The new reserve requirement will take effect on September 24, the bank said.

"This adjustment is intended to support prudent liquidity management and enhance the effectiveness of monetary policy transmission in line with the prevailing macroeconomic and financial sector developments," it said.

Adam Mugume, the central bank's executive director for research and policy, ruled out direct intervention through dollar sales to support the shilling, saying such a move would be "policy inconsistency".
In emailed comments to Reuters, he added that policymakers have sufficient tools at their disposal to contain exchange-rate volatility.
